name: Handler Hall
use: Residence hall (289 students), first-year and upper-division; InCEPSion engineering floor
style: Neo-traditional brick residence hall with cast-stone bands and gabled roofs (from photos)

facts.text: Built as SERC A (Southeast Residence Complex), opened 2007; renamed Handler Hall on October 11, 2013.

SERC was a three-building complex for 730 students built by Harvey Construction to designs by JSA, Inc.; SERC A is about 75,000 sq ft. Harvey first demolished nine existing two-storey buildings on the site; Phase 1 (A and B) finished by summer 2007, Phase 2 (C) by summer 2008.

Housing lists 289 students; traditional pod rooms plus suites: 32 traditional doubles, 4 traditional singles, 41 suites of two doubles and 8 suites of two doubles and two singles (excluding expanded-occupancy rooms).

Air conditioning, elevator, automatic front and rear doors, accessible private bathrooms on the 2nd and 4th floors; kitchen, laundry, lounges, sports courts. Home to the InCEPSion engineering learning-community floor.
Named for Evelyn E. Handler, UNH president 1980-83 and the first woman to lead any land- and sea-grant university.

s4.title: Ranking of UNH Dorms and Residence Halls

verdict: Big 2007 SERC hall in neat neo-traditional brick, with A/C and accessible baths; comfortable and anonymous.
notes: Commons photos: 2013 exterior shows a five-storey red-brick block with cast-stone banding, projecting gabled bays and a glazed corner stair; neat, conventional collegiate styling. 2025 entrance photo shows good-quality brick and wood doors. Harvey interior photo (lounge, hall unspecified) shows a curved carpeted lounge with large windows, standard ~8-9 ft acoustic-tile ceilings. Old row's "hotel feel" quote not re-verified.
judgeNotes: Photos show a conventional five-storey brick block; lounge reference is pleasant, rooms standard.
